title: Customer latency escalation: TTFT and tokens/sec regression across hosted/dedicated/private; implement tiered fallback hotfix
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported increased time-to-first-token (TTFT) and 20-40% drop in aggregate tokens/sec for a subset of model families after the 1.22 rollout of the kernel-scheduler heuristics. Impact spans Hosted API (region-us-west1), Dedicated pools with mixed GPU types, and two Private on-prem installs that pulled the update. Symptoms include long tail TTFT increases, spikes in GPU kernel queue time, and periodic KV cache invalidation events leading to recompile/quantization fallback paths.

Scope: Affects long-context generation workloads (seq_len > 1024) and batched small prompt workloads due to an interaction between the new kernel selection heuristic and our dynamic prefetch/prefix caching. Customers with bursty traffic (high qps with low tokens per request) see the worst throughput degradation.

Hypothesis / Root cause: The scheduler now prioritizes single-request low-latency kernels for short sequences; when mixed batches contain both short and long sequences, the kernel choice toggles leading to cache eviction and recompiles. This causes NVLink saturation in some Dedicated hosts when repeated context swaps occur, and a race in the KV cache eviction logic on Private deployments that restarts the memory manager too eagerly.

Immediate business need: Customers are escalating (one Enterprise customer is seeing a 35% increase in median TTFT and considering failover). We need a short-lived, safe hotfix that restores prior throughput characteristics while we finalize a more robust scheduling decision model.

Acceptance criteria for hotfix: 
- Median TTFT in affected workloads returns to within 5% of pre-1.22 baseline in hosted us-west1 and a representative Dedicated pool within 2 hours of rollout.
- Tokens/sec restores to >= 90% of baseline for mixed-batch workloads.
- No regressions in functional correctness or severe memory leaks in private installs.

Rollback plan: Canary hotfix to 5% of traffic in hosted, 1 Dedicated pool, and 1 Private pilot customer. Auto-rollback if error rate > 0.5% or TTFT degrades in canary after 15 minutes. Manual rollback steps documented in Confluence link (below).
